title: Poisoning, Chemicals & Overdose
summary: Get them away from the poison, call for advice, and keep any container or label. For suspected opioid overdose, give naloxone if available.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if they are unresponsive, drowsy, fitting or struggling to breathe
when: Unresponsive, very drowsy, or not breathing normally
Swallowed a corrosive, fuel or button battery
Gas, smoke or fumes affecting several people

steps.title: Protect yourself
steps.text: Do not enter a space with gas, smoke or fumes. Avoid contact with chemicals – wear gloves. Use the Hazmat lookup for placarded loads.

steps.title: Remove from the poison
steps.text: Move them to fresh air if it is safe. Remove contaminated clothing.

steps.title: Skin or eye contact
steps.text: Flush with large amounts of running water. For eyes, rinse with lukewarm water for at least 15–20 minutes, holding the eye open.

steps.title: Suspected opioid overdose
steps.text: If they are unresponsive with slow or no breathing (pinpoint pupils, drug use), call {EMERGENCY}, give naloxone if available as directed on the device, and start CPR if not breathing normally. Naloxone may need repeating.

steps.title: Get advice
steps.text: Call {POISON} or {EMERGENCY}. Keep the container, label, plant or tablets to show responders. Note what, how much and when.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Recovery position if unresponsive and breathing.

doNot: Do not give anything to eat or drink unless told to by poison control
Do not give mouth-to-mouth if the poison is on their lips – use a barrier
Do not enter a fume-filled area

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
